overview: From 2026-09-27 to 2026-10-04, ethereum-optimism/optimism had 43 new PRs (25 merged), 7 new issues, and 40 active contributors.

topIssues.title: Proofs: Increase `MAX_CLOCK_DURATION` and reduce air gap constants (keeping 7 day total) in preparation for faster withdrawals with ZK
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
The finality delay and the proof maturity delay are both constants, and the contract implementation is shared. So we can't reduce them for ZK and 1-day withdrawals if there are still other chains using fault proofs, since stage 1 requires 7 days in total. For example if `DISPUTE_GAME_FINALITY_DELAY_SECONDS` becomes 12 hours to provide fast withdrawals on ZK dispute games, then it would reduce FaultDisputeGame to 4 days total. 

To be configurable per-chain they would need to become constructor args. But aside from this transition period from fault proofs to ZK proofs, they don't really need to be configurable per chain.

Instead, we can reduce the finality delay (for all chains) to e.g. 12 hours, and increase `MAX_CLOCK_DURATION` to 6.5 days.

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: own the log layer — op-service/log becomes the monorepo logging API
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #21745 (§15 of the [op-geth decoupling doc](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md#L416-L436)). **Blocks #20266.**

`op-service/log` becomes the monorepo's logging API: no monorepo Go file imports `go-ethereum/log`. This is better layering regardless of the decoupling — the fork's `Logger.SetContext`/`WriteCtx`/`LogAttrs`/`Trace…ErrorContext` extensions are just what forces it.

## Scope (measured at 1657fbe)

- **697** monorepo Go files import `github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/log` — op-node 121, op-service 82, op-challenger 71, op-e2e 65, op-dispute-mon 48, op-test-sequencer 42, op-devstack 37, op-chain-ops 36, op-deployer 33, op-supernode 27, op-batcher 21, op-conductor 20, and a long tail. (`superchain-registry/` is a submodule with its own Go module — out of scope, flagged to that team.)
- **63** of those import *both* `geth/log` and `oplog`, so they need symbol-level dedup, not a blind import rewrite.
- Only ~13 files use the fork's context extensions at all: [`op-service/testlog`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-service/testlog/testlog.go), [`op-service/log/logfilter`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/tree/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-service/log/logfilter), `op-service/tls/tlsinfo.go`, `op-devstack/devtest`, plus a handful of call sites. Phase 2 is therefore small; phase 1 is the bulk.

## PRs

1. **`op-service/log`: add the `oplog` logger surface.** `type Logger = log.Logger` (alias) plus re-exports of the package-level API actually in use: `New`, `NewLogger`, `Root`, `SetDefault`, `With`, `Info/Warn/Error/Debug/Trace/Crit`, the `Level*`/`Lvl*` constants, `LevelFromString`, `FromLegacyLevel`, `DiscardHandler`, `NewTerminalHandler[WithLevel]`, `JSONHandler`, `LogfmtHandlerWithLevel`, `Handler`. Migrate `op-service` itself as the first consumer.
2. **Tree-wide sweep + gate.** Rewrite the remaining ~615 files to `oplog`, dedup the 63 dual-import files, and add a lint/CI gate (golangci `depguard`, or a grep check) that fails any new `go-ethereum/log` import. Pure rename while the alias holds — zero behaviour change; build + test is the gate. Land fast to avoid rebase churn against everything in flight.
3. **Flip the alias to an owned interface** *(at cutover)*. Replace the alias with an interface — upstream's method set plus the context methods — over an `slog`-backed implementation. Do **not** copy upstream's LGPL `log` package; the context-extension logic is OP-authored and ports over. Our interface is a superset of upstream's, so an `oplog.Logger` still satisfies `log.Logger` wherever we hand one into geth code (e.g. the in-process L1 geth in op-e2e).

PRs 1–2 land now and are independent of the rest of the epic. PR 3 lands with or just before the go.mod flip.

## Acceptance criteria

- No monorepo Go file imports `go-ethereum/log`, enforced by a CI/lint gate.
- `op-service/log/logfilter` and `op-service/testlog` build on the owned API with unchanged behaviour.
- After PR 3, `op-service/log` has no `go-ethereum/log` dependency, and an `oplog.Logger` is still accepted by geth APIs taking `log.Logger`.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5 (1M context)*

topPRs.title: op-private-interop!: establish the private-chain PoC reference
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Establishes an upstream draft reference for the private-chain interop PoC, including private execution, deterministic public projection, message-position resolution before publication, and persistent LightCL recovery. This is experimental work intended for eventual upstreaming after substantial review and refinement.

Projection spans are admitted as a whole before derivation releases their first new block. A pure Go/Kona validator enforces the transaction grammar, claim framing, per-block private OutputV0 records, and the span proof statement. After invalidation or sequencing-window expiry, publication binds to the canonical public parent and the last surviving private checkpoint, including a commitment to intervening replacement inputs. LightCL checks the local private output against the surviving record before adopting it, then retains its rewind, deposit-only replacement, and restart safeguards.

The verifier remains an explicitly configured insecure stub: publication is operator-attested, and private execution correspondence is not cryptographically verified. Protocol fallback blocks need no publisher proof; a future real proof must cover private execution through their recovery interval. This profile requires fresh deployments with interop and Isthmus active at genesis. Published spans cannot cross future activation blocks under the current rules. Initiating messages retain upstream's strict earlier-timestamp rule; same-timestamp dependencies remain unsupported. Private execution proofs, complete fault-proof execution support, and native ETH bridging/withdrawal settlement remain outside the supported profile.

Validation: targeted Go suites and repository Go lint pass; 662 affected Rust tests, strict clippy, no-std, feature propagation and SP1 guest lock checks pass; 31 private-profile Solidity tests plus three cross-language claim-vector tests pass. A fresh op-up private-interop smoke run passes. The full devstack/sysgo private-interop acceptance run passes all 13 enabled tests in 37m23s, including outage/expiry, invalidation, L1 reorgs, interrupted recovery, and restart after newer valid history. Changed registry artifacts and its interface pass scoped verification. Repository-wide contract tooling also encounters unchanged dispute-game interface mismatches and conflicting duplicate ZK-game build artifacts; those unrelated files are outside this update. The optional production-cadence soaks have not been repeated for this change. Two independent scoped reviews covered derivation parity, recovery, and public-source publication; broader production/security and full-feature reviews remain necessary.

Known existing CI issue: broad acceptance shards previously exposed the ordinary-follow finality guard rejecting stock EL-sync bootstrap snapshots whose follower finalized label is ahead of its source. That guard is unchanged by this update and remains an open issue for the recovery stack. Prior CI results do not establish that this revision is green.

This reference excludes atomic coordinator/shared-block builder work and local deployment artifacts. It does not update running devnet images.

**BREAKING CHANGE:** the new claim wire format, per-block output records, contract bytecode and private genesis-output configuration require matching clients/contracts and fresh databases. Preserve the private recovery journal alongside the private execution database. Unsupported private native bridge routes must remain disabled.

topPRs.title: op-reth!: demonstrate optimistic parallel execution PoC
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
This PoC explores reducing op-reth execution latency by speculating on independent transactions while preserving canonical transaction order, state, receipts, fees, and SDM settlement. It covers Engine validation, historical execution, forced transactions, pool sequencing, and subblock continuation. **Sequential execution remains the default; parallel and rolling execution are opt-in.**

The [PoC write-up](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/optimistic-parallel-execution/rust/op-reth/crates/parallel/POC.md) covers the high-level architecture, low-level decisions, results, and production gates. The [README](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/optimistic-parallel-execution/rust/op-reth/crates/parallel/README.md) documents configuration and reproduction commands.

The central choice is bounded speculation against immutable snapshots of **committed state only**. One coordinator validates dependencies and commits in order; stale or failed attempts execute once canonically. This avoids speculative worker-to-worker dependencies and cascading rollback. Independent worker-local readers remove coordinator read messages, and optional rolling scheduling overlaps ordered commit with further execution. Broker windows remain the compatibility fallback.

Protocol fee credits are settled in order without manufacturing dependencies between otherwise independent transactions. SDM observation is transaction-local; refund evaluation and policy updates remain ordered and commit-only. The authoritative selector controls inclusion, with `on_commit` before its next `next()`. Resource limits cover outstanding attempts, speculative gas, dependencies, outputs, and retained snapshot versions. Shared worker permits, generation checks, and reader-teardown barriers govern cancellation and competing operations.

| Synthetic comparison | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Final rolling vs sequential: independent compute | 3.1x at 4 workers; 4.4x at 8 |
| Final rolling vs sequential: stock BN254 pairings | 3.7x at 4 workers; 6.3x at 8 |
| Independent readers vs broker windows: storage | 5-6x at 4 workers |
| Rolling vs direct windows | 14-35% lower storage latency; 13% lower expensive-policy latency at 4 workers |

These are separate local in-memory experiments using an optimized test profile; their ratios are not cumulative. Cheap storage often remains faster sequentially. Contention, read amplification, retained snapshots, serial policy work, and tail latency limit the gains. No production database or end-to-end replay speedup is claimed. See the [performance report and raw data](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/optimistic-parallel-execution/rust/op-reth/crates/parallel/benchmarks/session-summary.md).

This draft depends on [ethereum-optimism/reth#10](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/pull/10). Before production: land reviewed source hooks; independently review and fuzz consensus-sensitive paths; replay representative chain ranges against known roots; measure release-build latency, memory, database I/O, and competing builds; integrate the real SDM policy; and complete shadow soak and canary rollout. Upstream borrowed/Arc configuration wrappers currently retain broker reads, and opaque Engine precompile-cache wrappers require canonical precompile fallback. Both remain documented compatibility limitations.

BREAKING CHANGE: Downstream Rust integrations constructing `OpBlockExecutionCtx` must supply `parallel_candidates` (empty for sequential execution) or use `..Default::default()`. Runtime-bearing executor factories and `OpExecutorBuilder` require explicit cloning instead of `Copy`; custom `OpTxEnv` implementations need `Clone`; generic `OpBlockExecutor` users must carry its `Evm` bound. Construct `OpHandler` with `OpHandler::new()` instead of external struct literals. No Engine API wire or database migration is introduced.

Validation: 603 affected execution/integration/txpool/CLI tests pass (3 skipped), including the rebased txpool affordability changes. The saved 121-configuration rolling benchmark checks output parity. Formatting, scoped Clippy with warnings denied, rustdoc, affected `no_std` builds, and the upstream-mirror check pass.

Rust correctness, deletion/write-preservation, and reth dependency/mirror reviews completed. Provider-failure propagation has regression coverage through actual EVM errors and cancellation races. The reth wrapper limitation above remains an open production follow-up. Full workspace `just lint` is blocked in the unchanged `gmp-mpfr-sys` dependency by missing `m4`; scoped checks are reported separately above.

Lagoon currently requires separate tools and pre-funded senders to exercise Interop and SDM together. `check-lagoon all` now takes one funded account, deterministically derives and tops up a separate SDM sender on both chains, then concurrently runs the complete Interop smoke suite and policy-producing SDM workloads on both chains; focused `sdm` subcommands remain available for generated or existing-block checks. Legacy nonzero PostExec `gasPrice` responses remain compatible, and `sdm-devnet` remains temporarily for existing Kupcake wrappers.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22988

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: add opt-in atomic ETH bridging PoC
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
Ordinary ETH bridging irreversibly locks the source before destination delivery. This PoC adds an optional safe mode that keeps native ETH refundable until the destination reserves mint capacity and the source commits. Existing `sendETH`/`relayETH` remain available; callers choose the three-message safe path through `initiateTransfer`.

Safe reservations have priority over ordinary relays, which must retry if unreserved capacity is insufficient. Both modes pay native ETH using existing ETHLiquidity. The acceptance fixture installs the experimental implementation behind the existing bridge predeploy on fresh test chains; production bridge code, messenger, inbox, and network upgrade bundles remain unchanged.

This demonstrates atomic asynchronous settlement, not synchronous execution or unconditional availability. Safety assumes canonical Interop histories, matching peer logic, and upgrades that preserve reservations. Committed transfers cannot be refunded if a chain disappears permanently. Live migration, reservation griefing, reorg/fault-proof testing, and expiry-resend integration remain production work. See the [design note](https://github.com/karlfloersch/optimism/blob/poc/safe-eth-bridge/packages/contracts-bedrock/docs/safe-eth-bridge.md) and [validation report](https://github.com/karlfloersch/optimism/blob/poc/safe-eth-bridge/packages/contracts-bedrock/docs/safe-eth-bridge-validation.md).

Go, contract/security, and documentation/coverage reviews completed; their actionable findings were fixed. No applicable review was skipped and no finding was dismissed.

Final validation: 35 new Foundry tests, 86 broader Interop tests, all three real two-L2 acceptance scenarios, and full Go lint pass. Earlier full contract runs pass (2,337 development / 2,397 optimized). The pre-PR runner passes 15 checks; its missing upgrade-script artifact is resolved by building scripts and rerunning that check successfully. The validation report records artifact/profile caveats, Slither advisories, and the reused op-reth binary.

CI: title, dependency review, and Wiz scanners pass. The [ARM image job](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/actions/runs/35276843548/job/105389902427) builds the package successfully, then fails provenance attestation with `missing "id-token" permission`; the x86 job is cancelled by the workflow. No CI configuration is changed here. The main fork CI suite still requires human authorization under repository policy.
